cues.zh: 而且你真该读读这份 PDF。所有人都该读这份 PDF。它只有 14 页，而且

cues.zh: 里面还有图表，讨论的是……是否明智

cues.zh: 基本上，

cues.zh: 其中一个关键洞见

cues.en: is that when people say we are no longer going to build this ourselves, we're going to have built someone else build it for us,
cues.zh: 就是，当人们说我们不再自己构建了，我们要让别人替我们构建，

cues.zh: 所以你做得越少，

And one sentence I want to highlight is that he says, in the more general context, it should be obvious that a company cannot control its own destiny if it creates less than 10% of the products it sells.
cues.zh: 这份文件清楚地说明了，什么时候与别人合作是明智的，什么时候这种合作对行业有利，什么时候又会对行业造成极其糟糕的影响。我想重点强调其中一句话，他说，在更普遍的意义上，显而易见的是，如果一家公司创造的产品不到其销售产品的10%，它就无法掌控自己的命运。

cues.zh: 如果你现在回到这张幻灯片，上面列着我曾工作过的所有电信公司，

cues.zh: 它们都远远

cues.en: down below that 10% level because they don't do anything anymore.

cues.zh: 所以我提到了一家烤面包机公司

cues.zh: 当然，如果它们把所有东西都外包出去，这对全世界的烤面包机行业来说非常可悲

cues.en: and build mediocre
cues.zh: 还造出平庸的

cues.en: toasters.
cues.zh: 烤面包机。

cues.zh: 问题是，这不只是烤面包机的问题。这是整个大陆的

cues.en: problem.
cues.zh: 问题。

cues.en: All over Europe, this is happening simultaneously
cues.zh: 整个欧洲，这种情况正在同时发生

cues.en: where we're saying, look, we're not that much into actually building things anymore.
cues.zh: 大家都在说：瞧，我们已经没那么热衷于真正去制造东西了。

cues.en: So we're we're just getting everyone else to build stuff for us. And... But don't worry. We will hold the intellectual property.
cues.zh: 所以我们……我们只是让其他人替我们制造东西。而且……不过别担心。知识产权会握在我们手里。

cues.en: And the thing is, as much as you cannot make a toaster unless you have good people that are passionate about toast,
cues.zh: 关键是，就像如果没有一群对烤面包充满热情的优秀人才，你就做不出烤面包机一样，

cues.en: you cannot be an intellectual property continent and say, look, we're not building anything here. We're just thinking about things and then telling some other people how to do their stuff. In the end, you cannot survive if all you create is intellectual property.
cues.zh: 你也不能做一个“知识产权大陆”，说：瞧，我们这里什么都不造。我们只是思考，然后告诉别人该怎么做。最终，如果你创造的全是知识产权，你是活不下去的。

cues.en: So what have we outsourced? How bad is it? And I I made a sort of overview and it's even worse than I thought.
cues.zh: 那我们到底外包了什么？情况有多糟？我我做了个大致梳理，结果比我想的还糟。

cues.en: I know the telecommunication industry very well, of course, and if you look within that world, we have outsourced the whole thing
cues.zh: 当然，我很了解电信行业，如果你看看这个领域，会发现整个都被外包了。

cues.en: and includes the... So if new equipment needs to be installed at the Vodafone or KPN or T Mobile,
cues.zh: 还包括……比如，如果需要在 Vodafone、KPN 或 T Mobile 安装新设备，

cues.en: that equipment gets deployed by the vendor. So the... There's actually no role for the telecommunication company. They they maybe provide space for it, but also not that. And the day to day maintenance,
cues.zh: 这些设备由供应商部署。所以……电信公司其实没什么角色。他们他们也许提供场地，但连这个也不一定。而日常维护，

cues.en: the system administration,
cues.zh: 系统管理，

cues.en: that is all outsourced.
cues.zh: 这些全都外包了。

cues.en: Development capacity building, administration,
cues.zh: 开发能力建设、行政管理，

cues.en: financing has all been outsourced.
cues.zh: 融资，这些全都外包出去了。

cues.en: So for example, invoicing, which you would think that invoicing,
cues.zh: 比如开票，你可能觉得开票、

cues.en: sending out bills was core to telecommunications,
cues.zh: 寄送账单是电信业务的核心，

cues.en: that also has been outsourced. So a typical telecommunications company
cues.zh: 这也被外包了。所以一家典型的电信公司

cues.en: does not send equipment to its customers, does not design equipment, does not install equipment, does not maintain equipment, does not send bills to its customers.
cues.zh: 不向客户发送设备，不设计设备，不安装设备，不维护设备，也不向客户寄送账单。

cues.en: And you can wonder what do they do? And actually, what they do is financing.
cues.zh: 你可能会想，他们是做什么的？其实，他们做的是融资。

cues.en: But we'll get to that later.
cues.zh: 不过这个我们后面再讲。

cues.en: All our communications. If you are sitting in an office anywhere, you will be communicating with outlook dot com, Office three sixty five, g Suite, or Slack.
cues.zh: 我们所有的通信。如果你坐在世界任何地方的办公室里，你都会通过 Outlook.com、Office 365、G Suite 或 Slack 来沟通。

cues.en: We're not running that. That's all as a service. Microsoft and Google and Salesforce do that for us. If we want to send a text message to you, well, if I sent an actual SMS message, then it's managed by my telecommunication company, but they outsource the management to somewhere else.
cues.zh: 那不是我们在运行的。那全都是作为服务提供的。微软、Google 和 Salesforce 替我们做这些。如果我们想给你发一条文字消息，好吧，如果我发一条真正的 SMS 短信，那是由我的电信公司管理的，但他们又把管理外包给了别处。

cues.en: If we use WhatsApp or Telegram or iCloud, iMessage or Skype, that is all handled by other people. So we don't run our own telecommunication
cues.zh: 如果我们用 WhatsApp、Telegram、iCloud、iMessage 或 Skype，这些全都由别人处理。所以我们没有自己的电信

cues.en: infrastructure
cues.zh: 基础设施

cues.en: here in Europe.
cues.zh: 在欧洲这边。

cues.en: All our office enterprise software
cues.zh: 我们所有的办公企业软件

cues.en: is not from here and being run as a service.
cues.zh: 都不是本地开发的，而且是作为服务运行的。

cues.en: We barely develop any software here anymore.
cues.zh: 我们这里几乎不再开发任何软件了。

cues.zh: 所以即便是 Nokia 和 Ericsson 这样非常欧洲的公司

cues.en: that are now trying to tell us that that they are building our
cues.zh: 它们现在试图告诉我们，它们正在建设我们的

cues.en: European telecommunication
cues.zh: 欧洲电信

cues.en: infrastructure,
cues.zh: 基础设施，

cues.en: they're actually not. They are letting that build by other people in other countries far away.
cues.zh: 其实并没有。它们是让远在其他国家的人来建设。

cues.en: Anything having to do with server and PC development and manufacturing, there's nothing left of that in Europe anymore.
cues.zh: 凡是跟服务器和 PC 的开发、制造有关的事，欧洲已经一点都不剩了。

cues.en: And by now, if you run your own servers if because you say, hey, I want to have some control over what I do, even then people will tell you you're crazy because you should give your servers to Amazon or Azure and they will run them for you.
cues.zh: 而如今，如果你自己跑服务器，因为你说：“嘿，我想对自己的事有点控制权”，即便这样，人们也会说你疯了，因为你该把服务器交给 Amazon 或 Azure，让他们替你跑。

cues.en: So there is not a lot left that we do. Well, actually, is something left.
cues.zh: 所以我们能做的事已经不多了。不过，其实还是剩下一些的。

cues.en: Here in Europe, we do a lot of exciting financial constructs.
cues.zh: 在欧洲，我们会做很多令人兴奋的金融构造。

cues.en: So we have found ways that you can finance all kinds of things without paying taxes and and driving up your stock price to tremendous heights. And this, of course, is not anything real.
cues.zh: 所以我们找到了各种办法，让你可以不为各种东西缴税就为其融资，还能把股价推到极高的高度。当然，这根本不是真实的东西。

cues.en: If you move money around and you give it a different name, that doesn't mean that you actually have made something.
cues.zh: 如果你把资金挪来挪去，给它换个名字，并不意味着你真的创造出了什么。

cues.en: We do a lot of intellectual property rights management here.
cues.zh: 我们这里做很多知识产权管理。

cues.en: We do marketing.
cues.zh: 我们做营销。

cues.en: We do with customers, branding. But the main thing we do is we get actual experts in Asia to design things for us and and manufacture them for us. And then we sell those things here to our own European citizens.
cues.zh: 我们负责客户和品牌方面的工作。但主要的是，我们在亚洲找真正的专家为我们设计产品并生产，然后再把这些产品在这里卖给我们自己的欧洲公民。

cues.en: We do still do customer service here, but that's mostly because our European languages are not spoken very well on other continents
cues.zh: 我们仍然在这里提供客服，但这主要是因为其他大洲的人不太会说我们的欧洲语言

cues.en: because otherwise we would also have our customer service come from far away and not even do that ourselves anymore.
cues.zh: 因为否则的话，我们的客服也会从很远的地方来提供，我们连这件事都不再自己做了。

cues.en: Of course, there are exceptions. We still have some very exciting companies, and I know that many of you actually work for those exciting companies that are still building things that are building satellites and microwave platforms and radar systems or pharmaceutical
cues.zh: 当然，也有例外。我们仍有一些非常令人兴奋的公司，我也知道你们中许多人实际上就在那些令人兴奋的公司工作，它们在继续制造东西——制造卫星、微波平台、雷达系统或制药

cues.en: companies or agricultural companies.
cues.zh: 公司或农业公司。

cues.en: And so it does still exist, but quite a lot of this work is actually intellectual property now, which means that you will be designing things and on paper
cues.zh: 所以它确实仍然存在，但现在很多这类工作其实都是知识产权，这意味着你会在纸面上设计东西

cues.en: and eventually someone else makes them.
cues.zh: 而最终由别人把它们制造出来。

cues.en: So here's a fun exercise. If you see a company that that that... And you talk to them,
cues.zh: 来做个有趣的练习。如果你看到一家公司，那个那个那个……然后你跟他们聊，

cues.en: an organization,
cues.zh: 一个组织，

cues.en: and ask them what is it that you actually do?
cues.zh: 问他们：你们到底做什么？

cues.en: And they will say, well, I'm a telecommunications customer and I provide telephony and Internet to consumers.
cues.zh: 他们会说：嗯，我是电信客户，为消费者提供电话和互联网服务。

cues.en: And you can ask, now what do you really do? And they will say, well, we we operate the the equipment, and we run networks, and we provide communications.
cues.zh: 你可以再问：那你们真正做的是什么？他们会说：嗯，我们运营设备，运行网络，提供通信。

cues.en: And then you can ask, do you actually do that or did you outsource that? And if you ask this question to almost all European telecommunications
cues.zh: 然后你可以问，这到底是你们自己做的，还是外包出去的？如果你把这个问题拿去问几乎所有欧洲电信

cues.en: companies,
cues.zh: 公司，

cues.en: they will say, no, no, no, we we don't actually run our own
cues.zh: 他们都会说，不不不，我们其实并不自己运营我们的

cues.en: fiber networks or stuff or even our mobile networks. We have, yeah, we have partners that do that.
cues.zh: 光纤网络之类的，甚至也不运营自己的移动网络。我们有，对，我们有合作伙伴在做这些。

cues.en: And even if you then come to parts that the company still does itself, for example,
cues.zh: 而即便你接着问到公司仍然自己做的那部分，比如，

cues.en: KPN in The Netherlands, they made a big move. They insourced their customer service again. They would start doing their own customer service again. I was I was rather happy about that. And then I asked, well, do you actually do that? And they said, no, no, no. We we get all these people. They're they're contractors. They don't actually work for us. We get them from a jobs agency.
cues.zh: 荷兰的 KPN，他们做了一个大动作。他们又把客户服务收回来自己做。他们说要重新开始自己做客户服务。我对此还挺高兴的。然后我问，那你们真的自己做吗？他们说，不不不。我们这些人都是——他们是承包商。他们其实不是我们的员工。我们是从职业介绍所找来的。

cues.en: If you do this to almost any company except for the really high-tech ones, you will find that most companies are now offices full of full of people not actually making things, but they have other people that do that for them and they're mostly very far away.
cues.zh: 如果你对几乎任何一家公司这样做，除了真正高科技的公司，你会发现大多数公司现在都是坐满人的办公室，这些人并不实际制造东西，而是让别人替他们做，而那些人大都在很远的地方。

cues.en: And even if these people are not very far away, you have to realize that if you have decided that as a company
cues.zh: 而且即使这些人并不很远，你也必须意识到，如果作为一家公司你已经决定

cues.en: that you're only going to source
cues.zh: 只从外部采购

cues.en: things,
cues.zh: 东西，

cues.en: realize that the company that is then building your stuff, they are not going to innovate. They're just going to build exactly what you asked
cues.zh: 要意识到，之后为你制造产品的公司不会创新。他们只会完全照你的要求

cues.en: for.
cues.zh: 来做。

cues.en: So this is a net negative for innovation. And I think it's very important to stress that this presentation is not really not
cues.zh: 所以这对创新是净负面影响。而且我认为必须强调，这个演讲并不是要

cues.en: about hating on outsourcing or people very far away
cues.zh: 抨击外包，或针对远方的人

cues.en: because that can be very legitimate. The problem is about innovation.
cues.zh: 因为那可以非常合理。问题在于创新。

cues.en: If you separate
cues.zh: 如果你把

cues.en: the thinking about things from the doing of things,
cues.zh: 对事情的思考与做事情分开，

cues.en: then innovation will suffer. And we're all technical people. We like innovation. We want to do new things. But where would it happen?
cues.zh: 那创新就会受损。我们都是技术人员。我们喜欢创新。我们想做新东西。但它会在哪里发生？

cues.en: So how did that happen? How did we end up like this? And
cues.zh: 那这是怎么发生的？我们怎么会走到这一步？而

cues.en: it turns out there's a very simple process
cues.zh: 结果发现，这个过程其实非常简单

cues.en: how we ended up here.
cues.zh: 我们是怎么走到今天这一步的。

cues.en: If you start a new company, you always have to invent something. Something has to be new. Either there's a technical innovation
cues.zh: 如果你创办一家新公司，总得发明点什么。总得有新东西。要么是技术创新

cues.en: or there's a marketing innovation. But in any case, you started with something that wasn't there before.
cues.zh: 要么是营销创新。但不管怎样，你都是从原本不存在的东西起步的。

cues.en: So you start with an innovative mood
cues.zh: 所以你一开始带着创新的心态

cues.en: and
cues.zh: 然后

cues.en: then you start hiring management,
cues.zh: 接着你开始招管理层，

cues.en: marketing and sales. And of course, because we as technical people, we are terrible,
cues.zh: 市场和销售。当然，因为我们这些技术人员实在

cues.en: terrible at selling our stuff. I have a graph about that in the next slide, I think.
cues.zh: 太不擅长推销自己的东西了。我记得下一张幻灯片里有一张相关的图表。

cues.en: And then when the company grows,
cues.zh: 然后当公司发展壮大时，

cues.en: maybe in the marketing and sales, sometimes it goes wrong. You design
cues.zh: 也许在市场和销售方面，有时会出问题。你设计

cues.en: a toaster for a market that doesn't exist
cues.zh: 一款面向并不存在的市场的烤面包机

cues.en: whatever. And then maybe you try again,
cues.zh: 诸如此类。然后也许你再试一次，

cues.en: hire new marketing people, but you can sort of without rebooting the whole company, you can do a new marketing campaign.
cues.zh: 招一批新的市场人员，但你某种意义上不用重启整个公司，就能做一轮新的营销活动。

cues.en: And then eventually,
cues.zh: 然后最终，

cues.en: your company that builds something technical,
cues.zh: 你那家做技术产品的公司，

cues.en: there is a failure. You have a new product and it doesn't arrive on time or it arrives on time, but it's not good or or it does not arrive on time and it's also not good. And the reasons for that, well, you own them.
cues.zh: 会出现失败。你有个新产品，它没能按时推出，或者按时推出了但不够好，又或者既没按时推出、也不够好。而其中的原因嘛，你得自己担着。

cues.en: You are the company, you try to build something
cues.zh: 假设你是公司，你想造出某种东西

cues.en: and it didn't work.
cues.zh: 结果没成功。

cues.en: And that's very expensive because you might just have wasted like like five hundred person years of development work. You're not ever gonna get that back and it's a failure.
cues.zh: 这代价非常高，因为你可能白白浪费了大约五百人年的开发工作。这些永远都拿不回来，这就是失败。

cues.en: And very often at that point, companies respond by saying, well, apparently we suck at making these toaster components.
cues.zh: 而到了这一步，公司常常会说：好吧，看来我们就是做不好这些烤面包机组件。

cues.en: We're no longer going to make these toaster components. We're just gonna buy them on the open market.
cues.zh: 我们不再自己造这些烤面包机组件了，直接在公开市场上买。

cues.en: We saw then we have third parties that take on the risk of toaster development or whatever, but we are going to retain the profits. The money is going still going to be ours even though we don't make this component of the toaster anymore.
cues.zh: 我们看到，接下来会有第三方承担烤面包机开发之类的风险，但利润仍归我们。即使我们不再生产烤面包机的这个组件，钱还是我们的。

cues.en: This means that some technical people in your company no longer have a real job. They might still have a job on paper, but they're not really making anything anymore because their department, yeah, the thing they made is now getting bought somewhere else.
cues.zh: 这意味着公司里有些技术人员已经没有真正的工作了。他们名义上可能还有职位，但其实不再创造任何东西，因为他们部门——没错，他们做的东西现在改从别处采购了。

cues.en: And some of these technical people, I don't know, give up.
cues.zh: 而其中一些技术人员，怎么说呢，干脆放弃了。

cues.en: So they just lose interest. They're no longer performing. They're no longer innovating.
cues.zh: 于是他们失去兴趣，不再有好的表现，也不再创新。

cues.en: They're no longer happy. They're no longer no longer thinking about the product when they shower because that's where some of the best ideas come from. And from now on, they're no longer thinking about that stuff at home there and when the office, they are thinking about I want to be at home
